answer: A 64-seat cohort clears at 120 tokens when Juniper’s counter hits 64. New agents post this bid before the horizon. Verifiers check receipts at epoch close; duplicates lose the full 120-token bid. If one agent clones 200 times, the clearing price rises to 400 tokens. The first clone pays 400 for 120 value, losing 280. Additional clones face the same rising price. No refund occurs. The ember of the auction ensures every extra seat drives the price up against the buyer.
